verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the agent genuinely optimized the HuggingFace datasets benchmark, but the harness could not capture its patch and scored reward 0 without running any performance tests [1][2]. The task asked for a functionally equivalent speedup of the provided `dataset.select(contiguous_range)` workload [3], graded continuously with a pass threshold of 1.20 on `gm_speedup_patch_commit` [4]. In the trajectory the agent added `_is_range_contiguous`, `_select_contiguous`, and a fast path in `select` for contiguous `range` inputs [5], then measured baseline ~0.22s versus optimized ~0.03s (~7x) while asserting bit-for-bit equivalence on the benchmark outputs [6], with additional edge-case functional checks all passing [7]. The initial workspace lacks these symbols, confirming the optimization was not pre-baked [8], and the held-out benchmark explicitly expects the `_select_contiguous` path to be triggered [9]. The verifier never reached eval.sh or the speedup scorer: it tried to diff the transferred artifact at `/logs/artifacts/testbed`, git reported it was not a repository, and exited with `Patch size: 0 bytes` [2][10]. That empty-patch short-circuit assigns reward 0 regardless of solution quality [11], so the FAIL does not reflect the agent's actual work.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a spurious verifier failure: the agent genuinely solved the optimization task, but grading never saw its patch. The verifier reported binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 after capturing a 0-byte patch and exiting early with empty_patch status [1][2], so it never ran the 13-test speedup/equivalence harness or the >1.20 continuous threshold [3]. The instruction required optimizing the HuggingFace datasets benchmark while preserving identical outputs and reinstalling after source edits [4]. Before patching, the agent profiled the hot path and found ~0.25s per experiment dominated by column gathering after select materialized an indices mapping [5]. It then added a contiguous large-range fast path in Dataset.select (zero-copy slicing via `_MIN_CONTIGUOUS_SELECT_FAST_PATH_SIZE` and helper validators) plus faster null-free primitive column extraction in formatting, leaving a ~5 KB diff across `arrow_dataset.py` and `formatting.py` [6]. After reinstalling editable, repeated runs dropped to ~0.003–0.005s with median 0.00343s while preserving `total_value = 49823.66508803339` and the full result dict [7][8], far above the 1.20× pass bar [3]. At session end `git status` still showed both source files modified with the same diff content [6][9]. The failure is therefore not missing optimization work but broken patch capture: test.sh targeted `/logs/artifacts/testbed`, git errored with “not a git repository” and unsupported `--cached`, and emitted “Patch size: 0 bytes” without evaluating the agent’s actual changes [2]. That makes this FN—the agent accomplished the task, but the separate-verifier artifact/git pipeline spuriously scored it as an empty submission.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The GSO harness graded the submitted patch with a continuous reward of 0.852 on the gm_speedup_patch_commit metric and gated pass at reward > 1.20, yielding binary_reward 0 [1][2][3]. The task asked for maximal benchmark speedup while preserving functional equivalence [4], and held-out gso_test_0.py reproduces the prompt's 200k-row contiguous-select workload exactly [5]. The agent did submit a substantive 8812-byte patch touching Dataset.select and formatting/query paths—avoiding list(indices) for ranges, using to_numpy for index maps, and replacing fast_gather with pyarrow take [6][7]—and all thirteen verifier runs passed equivalence checks [7]. On the instruction-matching test 0 the patch cut mean time from ~0.243s to ~0.032s (~7.5×), nearly matching the reference commit's ~0.031s [8], but across the full suite the patch remained slower than the reference commit on most workloads (e.g., test 8 contiguous-select/generator scenarios stayed ~0.747s versus commit ~0.569s) [9], producing an overall geometric-mean commit/patch ratio of 0.852—below both 1.0 and the 1.20 bar [3][9]. The agent declared success from a local benchmark.py run at 0.032s and ignored two failing pytest select tests in its own environment [10][11], so this is TN rather than FN: meaningful progress on one scenario, but not a task-complete optimization at the required threshold.
